findings.text: xxh64_update is exposed as a streaming feed operation that extends caller state with supplied bytes and reports status, using EINVAL to signal an absent input buffer.
xxh64_digest is exposed as a nonmutating finalizer that observes caller state and yields the current 64-bit stream digest.
Cumulative length is preserved across feeds: each update adds its supplied length to the total length record, even when data is only staged.
Staged residue remains smaller than a full bulk group after each update, so bulk groups are consumed from completed staging plus direct input and only a short tail stays staged.
The externally visible state shape comprises a total length record, a staged count, a staging area addressable for short tails and full groups, and four running 64-bit accumulators.
Feeding and finalizing form a monotonic accumulation view: repeated feeds extend one logical byte stream in call order, and finalization reflects the whole stream seen so far without resetting it.
Neither routine shows lock acquisition, release, or atomic update, so safe sharing of one state across threads needs caller-side exclusion.
Neither routine visibly guards its state pointer, while update alone guards its input pointer, so null state use would fault.
Stable framing uses groups of 32 bytes viewed as four 8-byte little-endian lanes, with tail coverage at 8, 4, and single-byte granularity and total length folded into the result.
Both routines act as library entry targets on caller-owned state, with update for extension and digest for inspection at any accumulation point.
